propositions: Full ticket-store materialization currently requires 135–235 seconds and scales with inode tree work across 5,500 directories and 132,000 files.
Capturing an immutable tracker commit OID and reading Git objects lazily can reduce scoped single-ticket extraction to ~29 ms, 4,600–8,000 times faster than full-store materialization.
Pinned reads from a captured commit OID remain byte-identical while concurrent mutations advance the live tracker to a new commit, proving isolation without full copies.

Scoped Git-plumbing reads must track exact-object dependencies and predicate dependencies (e.g., children-of-target) separately; unrelated mutations validate the predicate, but target mutations or child additions invalidate it.

Reducer-ignored fields like COMPLETION_VERDICT and updated_at can cause target-tree OID changes that invalidate raw hash equality; validation must distinguish state-bearing inputs from operation-owned observability events.
Read-only views must carry canonical references or resolver context to avoid alias-resolution discrepancies between scoped and full-store reductions.
